coverage.notes: SEL: DPI's 'Wisconsin PK-Adult Social and Emotional Learning Competencies' (May 2018): 24 numbered competencies in 3 domains with benchmarks for six grade bands (4K-5K, 1-3, 4-5, 6-8, 9-10, 11-adult). Read the English PDF linked from the DPI page. DPI calls these 'competencies', not 'standards', and the guide does not say whether use is required; I chose k12_standards because they are state-issued, grade-banded benchmarks (same call as NY's voluntary benchmarks) - reviewer may prefer guidance_only. Portrait of a Graduate: the DPI page says a statewide Portrait is being developed with AASA through a 5-phase process running October 2025 to October 2026 (listening sessions done, draft not yet published on the page). No attributes were published, so no POG framework was added. Reviewer: re-check the POG page; it may be finalized by or after this date.

frameworks.name: Wisconsin PK-Adult Social and Emotional Learning Competencies
frameworks.notes: Read from DPI's PDF 'Social and Emotional Learning Competencies' (May 2018), https://dpi.wi.gov/sites/default/files/imce/sspw/pdf/SEL-Competencies-Guide-web.pdf (same file as the English link /media/40286/download?inline on the DPI page; text compared and identical). Three Wisconsin domains: Emotional Development (1-6), Self-Concept (7-11), Social Competence (12-24). The PDF gives no short titles - only a domain heading plus a grade-band statement per number - so the titles here are MY paraphrased labels and the summaries blend the six grade-band statements; reviewer should check them against the chart (PDF pages 18-25). caselCompetency is set only where the guide's CASEL Domain column lists a single domain; competencies 9, 11, 22, 23, 24 list two or more domains and 4 is labeled 'Focus Attention' (not a CASEL domain), so those are left blank. Items use the guide's own numbers. 'Adopted' year is the publication year; the guide does not describe a formal adoption.

items.title: Recognizing and labeling emotions
items.summary: Notice and name one's own and others' feelings, moving from basic to complex and changing emotions, and see how this shapes thinking and relationships.

items.title: Expressing emotions appropriately
items.summary: Express feelings in words and actions that fit the setting and audience, and understand how that expression affects how others respond.

items.title: Managing strong emotions
items.summary: Use calming and coping strategies for stress and impulses, progressing from adult-guided support to anticipating and planning for triggering situations.

items.title: Focusing attention
items.summary: Use organizational skills and strategies to hold attention despite distractions and work toward short-term, then long-term, personal and academic goals.

items.title: Empathy and compassion
items.summary: Read how others feel, respond with comfort and respect, and grow toward showing connection and empathy for communities.

items.title: Predicting others' feelings and cues
items.summary: Link words, gestures, and situations to others' emotions, use perspective-taking to predict feelings and the effect of one's own behavior, and read social and cultural cues.

items.title: Strengths and growth mindset
items.summary: Recognize strengths and areas needing help, use a growth mindset, and set priorities for building skills and overcoming barriers.

items.title: Beliefs, values, and reflection
items.summary: Identify one's own beliefs and values, compare them with others', and reflect on whether behavior matches them.

items.title: Family, culture, and identity
items.summary: Understand how family, culture, and community roles shape identity, thoughts, and actions, and how one's beliefs affect growth.

items.title: Setting and tracking goals
items.summary: Set realistic personal and academic goals, monitor progress, and adjust plans, extending to group goals in later grades.

items.title: Persistence and learning from setbacks
items.summary: Try new things, keep going after setbacks, spot barriers and supports, and show perseverance through adversity.

items.title: Perspective-taking and respect for viewpoints
items.summary: Understand and respect other people's points of view, express one's own, and use conversation to learn others' perspectives.

items.title: Respecting family, culture, and community
items.summary: Find commonalities, build relationships across groups, and support everyone's right to express family, culture, and community identity.

items.title: Difference, bias, and discrimination
items.summary: Respect individual differences, understand how stereotypes harm, identify discrimination, and assess personal bias.

items.title: Building healthy relationships
items.summary: Form and keep healthy relationships, recognize the costs of unhealthy ones, and use boundaries and warning signs to avoid them.

items.title: Communication and assertiveness
items.summary: Start conversations, listen, and communicate clearly, building to assertive communication, including refusals, that meets needs without harming others.

items.title: Adapting to and giving feedback
items.summary: Adapt behavior to adult direction, peer feedback, and environmental cues, and accept and later offer constructive feedback.

items.title: Cooperation and teamwork
items.summary: Take part in cooperative play and group work, set shared goals, overcome disagreements, and recognize each member's contribution.

items.title: Conflict resolution
items.summary: Communicate needs in conflict, understand others' perspectives and causes, apply negotiation and resolution skills, and reflect on one's own role.

items.title: Making responsible choices
items.summary: Recognize choices, generate options, weigh consequences for oneself and others, and apply a systematic decision process with ethical and safety factors.

items.title: Social norms and expectations
items.summary: Follow group rules and school expectations, and understand how social norms vary by setting and culture and are shaped by public opinion.

items.title: Personal health and safety
items.summary: Understand safety rules, describe ways to stay safe, use refusal and negotiation skills against unwanted pressure, and protect personal and community health.

items.title: Seeking help and self-advocacy
items.summary: Learn to get help from trusted adults, offer help to others, and advocate for one's own and others' needs using support networks.

items.title: Contributing to the community
items.summary: Notice classroom, school, and community needs, plan actions that address them, and later engage in civic activity to improve communities.
